html:
A tropical cyclone that struck Burma on 2 May 2008 and drove a storm surge deep into the Irrawaddy delta, killing about 140,000 people. It was the worst natural disaster in the country's recorded history.

The delta is low, flat and crowded with rice farms and fishing villages. The surge pushed sea water some 40 kilometres inland, sweeping away whole townships. Millions lost homes, crops and boats.

The military government made the disaster worse. It was slow to warn people and, fearing foreign influence, it kept out most international aid workers and turned away foreign navy ships loaded with supplies. Days after the storm it went ahead with a referendum on a new constitution designed to keep the army in power. Only after weeks of pressure, with help from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, did it let more aid in.

The storm came less than a year after the army crushed the Saffron Revolution of Buddhist monks. Its handling of Nargis deepened distrust of the regime at home and abroad, as with other great storms such as Typhoon Haiyan.
sum: A tropical cyclone that struck Burma on 2 May 2008 and drove a storm surge deep into the Irrawaddy delta, killing about 140,000 people. It was the worst natural disaster in the country's recorded history.
